result: ⛔ RESOLVED IN TRADINGVIEW'S FAVOUR - the contested V1 row was a false negative

action: Look for a redo control in the toolbar, then long-press the undo arrow
response: There is NO redo control anywhere in the mobile chart toolbar - the toolbar carries a single back arrow. Long-pressing it produced no menu; it simply behaved as another undo tap, stepping back a second time (removing the placement) after which the arrow greyed out.
result: ⭐ MOBILE HAS UNDO AND NO REDO - the history is one-way
notes: ⭐ SIGNIFICANT, AND IT CUTS AGAINST TRADINGVIEW. The desktop toolbar carries BOTH arrows (verified on tradingview.com in the same session). The phone gets only undo. Consequence measured directly: after undoing twice the stack was exhausted and the arrow disabled, so the placement could not be replayed - an accidental undo on a phone is UNRECOVERABLE. Classify as DESKTOP_ONLY for redo. ⭐ UCT IS AHEAD HERE: its MobileDrawBar carries Undo AND Redo side by side (UCT-DRAW-0001).

target: Trash in the floating style toolbar

response: The drawing was deleted immediately. NO confirmation dialog, no toast, no undo snackbar.
result: SINGLE-DRAWING DELETE IS UNCONFIRMED AND SILENT

Given there is no redo (UNDO-0002), a mis-tapped trash costs the object and one undo tap is the only recovery - and only if the user notices in time.

target: Selection handle and floating style toolbar

response: The object is placed and IMMEDIATELY SELECTED: a hollow rounded-square handle renders on the line, a price badge (737.64) appears on the price scale, and a floating toolbar docks above the object with EIGHT controls - drag grip, templates, colour (with a colour underline), text, '1px' width, line style, trash, and an overflow. The BOTTOM toolbar simultaneously switches into drawing mode with six controls: active tool, magnet, keep-drawing, visibility, layers, fullscreen.
result: ⭐⭐ PLACEMENT AUTO-SELECTS AND IMMEDIATELY OFFERS STYLE PLUS DELETE, WITHOUT A LONG-PRESS
notes: ⭐⭐ RESOLVES FOUR INFERRED ROWS AT ONCE - DRAW-0020 (handles), DRAW-0029 (colour), DRAW-0030 (thickness), DRAW-0031 (line style) - and it materially REFINES PRIMITIVE P1. TradingView's horizontal line is ALSO tap-to-place, exactly like UCT's. The difference is what happens NEXT: TradingView hands you a handle and a style bar in the same gesture, so the tap is a DRAFT you immediately adjust, whereas UCT's tap is a COMMIT you must delete and retry. ⛔ Do not restate P1 as 'TradingView drags, UCT taps' - that is too crude. The accurate statement is: BOTH place by tap; TradingView makes the result immediately adjustable and UCT does not. (UCT does have a DrawingQuickBar on coarse-pointer devices which my desktop-frame harness could not exercise - see UCT-METHOD-0001 - so this comparison is not final until UCT is tested on real touch.)

action: Open the Analysis hub in landscape and compare its bands against portrait
response: The hub renders as a LEFT-ANCHORED PANEL occupying roughly the left half, with the chart still visible beside it. Bands present: layout row (Layout setup / Manage <layout> / Chart settings), layout row 2 (New / Save / Open), 'Trade with your broker', then MORE. ⭐ THE ENTIRE 'TOOLS' BAND IS ABSENT.
result: ⭐⭐ THE HUB SHEDS ITS TOOLS BAND IN LANDSCAPE BECAUSE THE TOOLBAR ABSORBED IT
notes: ⭐⭐ THE MOST ELEGANT ADAPTIVE-DESIGN FINDING IN THE TEARDOWN. The hub is not a fixed menu that reflows - its CONTENTS are a function of what the toolbar can already reach. Rotate to landscape and the seven TOOLS tiles vanish from the hub because all seven became toolbar buttons; what remains is exactly what the toolbar cannot host (layout management, broker, long tail). That is a genuinely sophisticated answer to 'how do you avoid two doors to the same thing', and it is the direct counter-example to UCT's fixed five-door toolbar plus fixed eleven-row Tools sheet, which are identical in every orientation.

On Save, a NEW layout opened carrying the SAME SYMBOL (SPY, 1D) but with indicators and panes RESET to defaults - the uct-oracle pane from the previous layout was gone.
result: ⭐ NEW LAYOUT KEEPS THE SYMBOL AND RESETS EVERYTHING ELSE, AND DEMANDS A NAME UP FRONT
notes: NEW ROW, and it completes the LAYOUT lifecycle: Open (LAYOUT-0001), Save/auto-save (LAYOUT-0023), New (here). The naming prompt is the interesting half - TradingView refuses to create an anonymous workspace, which is why its layout list stays navigable at seven entries with duplicate names (LAYOUT-0001). Contrast: the one 'Unnamed' row in that list dates from 2024, so this dialog appears to be newer than the anonymous-layout era. ⭐ This flow is also the safe research protocol: an isolated named layout is two taps away, which is how all V2 mutation testing was kept off the owner's real layouts.
